transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to convene this group because we have a research agreement with Northbridge University that's approaching execution, and per company policy, we need to clear the IP, grant-compliance, product, and export-control terms before we sign. I've reviewed the current draft, and I have some concerns I'd like to work through with all of you. First, the draft is silent on export controls entirely — there's no export-control provision at all. Given that this is a battery-inverter research project, I want to make sure we address that. Second, the draft permits publication after a 60-day review period, and I want to discuss whether that's sufficient from a product and IP perspective. Third, the IP structure has project improvements jointly owned, with the company getting a worldwide, nonexclusive license to commercialize project results — I want to make sure that works for our product team. And finally, I want to confirm we're thinking about grant compliance, since university research often involves federal funding conditions. Who'd like to start?

Maya, the export-control issue is clear — we cannot execute without a provision establishing that no controlled technical data under ECCN 3A001 will be released to university researchers until export-license review is completed and any required licenses are obtained. Can you draft that clause?

Given all of this, it's apparent we have substantial revisions needed across IP ownership, license scope, grant compliance, and export controls before this agreement can be cleared per company policy. I'd like each of you to come back with your proposed language or schedules, and then we can review the revised draft together. Does that approach work for everyone?
